skip_reasons: TestCreateFailsClosedWithoutBuildIdentity: this go test binary is itself built with the toolchain's default VCS stamping, so resolveBuildSHA's runtime-metadata fallback always succeeds here and the true fail-closed path (no explicit SHA and no embedded VCS revision) cannot be driven end-to-end in this environment; the fail-closed branch itself is short, direct code in resolveBuildSHA and is covered by the other Create tests exercising the non-empty-buildSHA path.

acceptance.criterion: Truncated/tampered DB/bundle/manifest, duplicate/omitted/unknown brain, unsupported schema and unsafe path all fail before reactivation.
acceptance.expected: Every listed corruption/tamper class is rejected before any bytes are published to the restore destination.
acceptance.observed: Fixture tests cover: truncated/tampered control.db and bundle (checksum/length), truncated and legacy-v1 manifest, tampered bundle head recorded in the manifest, unknown brain (renamed ID) and omitted brain (dropped manifest entry) against the restored control database, schema-version mismatch between manifest and artifact (checked read-only before store.Open can migrate), and a symlinked control.db/bundle/manifest.json. Every case leaves no destination directory at all (os.Stat confirms ErrNotExist). Fixture/local-process evidence only.

acceptance.criterion: Manifest roundtrip matches exact fact IDs and canonical bundle heads; restored raw credentials/sessions remain invalid.
acceptance.expected: A create-then-restore round trip reproduces identical canonical content and exact bundle heads (including the bundle's own HEAD entry), and restored client_credentials/sessions/oauth_* state is revoked or cleared.
acceptance.observed: TestCreateRestoreRoundTrip verifies manifest brain IDs/heads and restored file content/heads match exactly (via git show-ref plus a resolved HEAD, matching git bundle list-heads' own HEAD+refs/heads/* shape). TestRestoreRevokesCredentialsAndOAuthState verifies a restored client_credentials row is revoked; existing oauth_grants/codes/consents/sessions/login_tokens clearing logic is unchanged from the prior implementation. Round-trip content used a representative committed file rather than the product's internal/writer.MemoryFact path (see limitations); bundling is content-agnostic so this is a reasonable proxy, not identical to the real remember pipeline.

acceptance.criterion: Live write during coordinated backup is either included consistently or excluded as a later operation; no acknowledged pre-snapshot write lost.
acceptance.expected: A dirty (uncommitted) canonical working tree at backup time is flushed into the snapshot rather than silently dropped by `git bundle`, or Create fails rather than bundling an inconsistent tree.
acceptance.observed: TestCreateFlushesDirtyCanonicalStateBeforeBundling leaves an uncommitted write in a brain's working tree, runs Create, and verifies the restored snapshot contains the flushed content and the source tree is clean afterward. Fixture/local-process evidence only; no live concurrent-writer race was exercised since no real service/gateway process was run.

limitations: buildSHA/journal wiring into internal/hosted/service/service.go and internal/cli/hosted.go is submitted as an integration request, not applied by this task (both files are outside R-hosted-backup's write scope).
No production contracts.DeletionJournal implementation exists yet (task48 is not started); Create/Request cannot be exercised against a real deletion journal, only the test-only fakeJournal fixture.

A ready brain with no canonical Git repository now fails backup as corruption unconditionally, including a freshly signed-up, never-connected brain -- today's provisioning (provision.finish) can produce exactly that state before pool.Acquire's lazy git-init ever runs. This is a cross-owner provisioning gap (T23.46/pool), recorded in integration-request.md, not something this task's write scope can fix.
Round-trip content tests use a representative committed file, not the product's real internal/writer.MemoryFact write/remember path.

service.go's existing service_test.go/oauth_test.go call backup.Restore (unchanged signature) and would need a corresponding backup.Create/Request update wherever they or Service.Backup are exercised after the integrator applies the signature change; this task did not run those out-of-scope suites.
